short_description.en: Siddhak cow dung cakes (gau kande) are made from desi cow dung and sun-dried without chemicals, for havan, yajna, agnihotra and daily pooja. Burning them in the home is traditionally believed to invite the blessings of Goddess Lakshmi.

long_description.en:
Siddhak cow dung cakes (gau kande / gobar ke uple) are prepared from pure, naturally dried desi cow dung for Hindu rituals, havan, yajna, agnihotra and daily pooja.

In Sanatan Dharma the cow (Gau Mata) is deeply revered, and the five cow products known as Panchgavya (milk, ghee, curd, gomutra and gobar) are considered sacred. As per Hindu belief, Goddess Lakshmi resides in cow dung, and using it in pooja, havan and agnihotra is believed to invite her blessings. That is why village and traditional homes still use cow dung to purify courtyards on festivals like Diwali, prepare the havan kund fire and perform Agnihotra at sunrise and sunset.

What makes them special

- Made from pure desi cow dung: no chemicals, no artificial binders, no synthetic fragrance
- Naturally sun-dried and shaped using age-old methods
- Made to burn steadily and evenly
- Easy to light with a little ghee, camphor or a cotton wick

Benefits

- Gentle, earthy fragrance that suits mantra chanting, meditation and worship
- Traditionally believed to purify the environment on a subtle level
- Believed to invite Goddess Lakshmi's blessings of prosperity and harmony (a matter of faith and tradition)
- Biodegradable and eco-friendly, free from synthetic fuels
- After use, the ash is often added to home gardens as a traditional soil additive

Ideal for

- Havan / yajna at home, temple or ashram
- Agnihotra (morning and evening fire ritual)
- Navratri, Diwali, Durga Pooja, Lakshmi Pooja, Govardhan Pooja, Satyanarayan Katha
- Griha Pravesh and vastu shanti
- Shraddh, Pitru Tarpan and festive poojas
- Daily pooja fire for dhupa, aahuti or simple flame offerings

How to use

- Havan / yajna: place 2–4 cakes in the havan kund, add a few dry wood sticks or cotton wicks, light with a diya or matchstick, and once the fire is steady offer ghee and havan samagri while chanting mantras.
- Daily pooja / Lakshmi pooja: light a small piece or one full cake in a safe fireproof container, let it settle into embers, then offer dhoop, flowers and aarti.
- Agnihotra (with proper guidance): place a small portion in a clean copper pyramid or agnihotra vessel, light it a few minutes before sunrise or sunset, offer ghee and materials as per agnihotra vidhi, and chant the mantras.
- Always follow the guidance of your family priest, guru or ritual expert for specific ceremonies.

Storage and safety

- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture.
- Keep away from children and pets.
- Always burn on a non-flammable surface or in a havan kund, with proper ventilation indoors.
- Never leave a burning fire unattended.

Sizes and packs

- Small (2 inch): Pack of 84, Pack of 504, and bori (sack) packs
- Big (3 inch): Pack of 12

short_description.en: Siddhak Janeu for puja: Yajnopavita sacred threads made from soft, durable cotton for Upanayanam, Sandhya Vandana and Hindu rituals. Available in packs of 20, 40 and 80 pieces for families, temples and priests.

long_description.en:
Siddhak Janeu for puja (also called Yajnopavita, Yagyopavit, Janeyu or sacred thread) is one of the most revered symbols in Sanatana Dharma. Worn across the left shoulder and resting on the right side, the Janeu represents purity, discipline, responsibility and a life dedicated to Dharma.

It is first worn at the Upanayana (sacred thread ceremony) and is then worn during daily Sandhya Vandana, Gayatri japa, homas, yajnas and all major Hindu rituals. Our Janeu is made with high-quality cotton threads, twisted and knotted in the traditional way.

Meaning and tradition

- Symbol of the "twice-born" (Dvija): the Upanayanam marks a second birth into spiritual learning, Vedic study and righteous conduct.
- The three strands are interpreted as body, mind and speech; sattva, rajas and tamas (the three gunas); or the duties owed to Devas, Rishis and Pitris.
- Worn daily, it is a reminder to live a disciplined life, follow one's dharma, chant the Gayatri mantra and stay connected to the Divine.

Benefits

- Traditional design and proportions: made following customary Vedic guidelines for length, knotting and number of strands
- High-quality cotton thread: soft on the skin, strong enough for everyday use
- Sacred knot (Brahma Granthi) tied in the traditional manner
- Lightweight and comfortable for daily wear during work, study, prayer and meditation
- Ritual-ready and clean for homas, yajnas, vratas, festivals and temple visits

Ideal for

- Upanayana / sacred thread ceremony (Yajnopavita samskara)
- Daily Sandhya Vandana, Gayatri mantra japa and nitya karma
- Priests (purohits), devotees, temples and household havan, yagya, homa and vratas
- Griha Pravesh, Vivah (wedding rituals), Pitru pooja, Satyanarayan pooja, Navratri, Diwali Lakshmi pooja
- Wearing or renewing on Upakarma, Raksha Bandhan, Janmashtami, Navaratri, Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali

How to use

- Traditionally worn over the left shoulder and across the chest, resting on the right side.
- Usually worn after snana (bath) and sankalpa, as per family or Guru's tradition.
- Many families change the Janeu every year on Upakarma or during specific festivals.
- Change it if it becomes impure, damaged or worn out, as per traditional guidelines.

Care

- Hand wash gently in clean water when required; avoid harsh detergents and vigorous wringing.
- Keep in a clean, dry place away from dust when not in use.

Pack sizes

- 20 pcs
- 40 pcs
- 80 pcs

long_description.en:

Traditionally tied on the wrist during pooja, homa and festivals, Kalawa is believed to invoke divine blessings, protection and good fortune.

The 10 metre roll gives ample length for family rituals, temple use, festivals, home pooja and spiritual gatherings.

Meaning and tradition

- Raksha Sutra: often tied on the wrist by a priest or elder while chanting mantras, as a sacred bond of protection and blessings.
- Red signifies strength, energy, Shakti and auspiciousness; yellow represents purity, wisdom and the grace of Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi.
- It is usually tied after taking a sankalpa, as a reminder to stay committed to one's prayers and vows.

Benefits

- 10 metre continuous roll for many poojas, functions, temple rituals and festivals
- Traditional red-yellow colour combination
- High-quality cotton: soft on the skin, strong for wrist-tying and decoration, easy to cut and tie
- Rolled format: cut only the length you need and keep the rest neat and tangle-free

Common uses

- Wrist-tying (Raksha Sutra): in many traditions on the right wrist for men and unmarried boys, and on the left wrist for women and girls
- Ganesh pooja, Satyanarayan Katha, Navratri and Durga pooja, Lakshmi pooja and Diwali, Hanuman pooja, Shiv pooja, homas and havans
- Tying around the kalash at griha pravesh, weddings and major ceremonies
- Wrapping coconuts, the pooja thali and deity photos or idols
- Griha Pravesh, weddings and engagements, thread ceremonies, naamkaran and other samskaras
- Navratri, Diwali, Raksha Bandhan, Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi, temple rituals and satsangs
- Offering in temples and tying to sacred trees, railings or mandir doors
- Daily pooja and yajnas by priests (purohits) and pandits
- New beginnings: new home, new vehicle, shop opening, exams, business start

How to use

- During pooja: take a small length, hold it during sankalpa, and the priest or elder ties it on the wrist while chanting mantras.
- For kalash and pooja setup: cut the length you need and wrap it around the kalash, coconut or pooja chowki, or use it to decorate the thali and bind small sacred items.
- For daily and festival use: keep the roll in your home mandir and tie fresh Kalawa on important days, vratas and new undertakings.

Care and storage

- Store in a clean, dry place, preferably with your pooja items, away from moisture and dust.
- Use clean scissors to cut the required length.

Pack sizes

- 10 m

long_description.en:
Siddhak Pure & Organic Hawan Samagri is a sacred blend prepared to an authentic Vedic formulation with 51 natural ingredients, including herbs, aromatic woods, resins, roots, leaves and flowers known for their spiritual and cleansing properties.

Unlike mixtures that rely on artificial fragrance or chemical fillers, our hawan samagri is 100% chemical-free. When you open the pack, the herbs and other ingredients are clearly visible and identifiable.

Benefits

- 51 natural ingredients, selected with care and respect for tradition
- Releases a soothing, earthy aroma when offered in havan or puja
- Traditionally believed to purify the surroundings, remove negative energy and invite peace, prosperity and blessings
- Finely hand-processed: easy to handle, light and burn evenly without excessive smoke or residue
- Chemical-free, for those who prefer traditional, earthy fragrances over synthetic scents
- Each pack is sealed to keep the aroma and ingredients fresh

Ideal for

- Daily home puja
- Special havan ceremonies
- Festival rituals: Diwali, Navratri, Durga Puja, Holi and more
- Temple offerings
- Housewarming rituals and Vastu purification
- Wellness sessions, meditation and yogic practice

Pack sizes

- 500 g: for frequent havans, families and small temples

short_description.en: Siddhak Rose Petals freshener spray fills your home mandir with the soft aroma of fresh roses, inspired by the rose offerings made to Mata Ji and Lord Ganesha. Use before Navratri, Ganesh pooja, daily aarti and festivals; in 50 ml and 100 ml.

long_description.en:
Siddhak Rose Petals freshener spray is made for devotees of Mata Ji (Durga, Ambe, Vaishno Devi, Lakshmi, Santoshi, Kali) and Lord Ganesha. It captures the fragrance of fresh rose petals, one of the most loved flowers in Hindu worship.

Rose (gulab) is offered to the Divine Mother in garlands and decorations during Navratri, Durga Ashtami and other Devi poojas, and stands for love, devotion, shakti and beauty. For Lord Ganesha, roses are common in Ganesh sthapana, aarti and visarjan, and pair well with modak and laddoo prasad.

Benefits

- Classic rose petals fragrance: fresh, floral and lightly sweet, not a harsh synthetic perfume
- Prepares your pooja room before worship and helps neutralise everyday smells (kitchen, closed rooms, dust)
- Instant temple-like ambience when guests arrive for pooja, bhajan or katha
- Non-messy way to refresh the mandir, for flats where burning a lot of dhoop is not possible
- Fragrance is subjective; intensity can vary by person and room

Ideal for

- Daily morning and evening aarti
- Navratri, Durga Pooja, Ashtami, Mata ki Chowki, Jagran and bhajan sandhya
- Tuesday and Friday Devi pooja
- Ganesh Chaturthi, Sankashti, Ganesh sthapana, aarti and visarjan, and new beginnings at home, office or shop
- Diwali, Karva Chauth, Teej, special vrats and sankrantis
- Living rooms before bhajans, meditation and japa corners, reading corners
- Gifting for Navratri or Ganesh Chaturthi visits, Griha Pravesh and new mandirs

How to use

- Clean the altar and arrange Mata Ji's photo or murti, or the Ganesh murti, with flowers, durva, chunri, diya and prasad.
- Shake gently if needed, hold the bottle upright and spray 3–6 times into the air, around the room and near (not directly on) the mandir.
- Lightly mist curtains and corners from a safe distance for a lingering aroma.
- Wait a minute for it to settle, then light the diya and begin aarti ("Jai Ambe Gauri", "Aigiri Nandini", "Om Gan Ganapataye Namah" or "Vakratunda Mahakaya").
- At a chowki or jagran, spray before guests arrive and lightly again during breaks.

Care and safety

- Do not spray directly on idols or photos of deities, on diyas, candles, agarbatti or any open flame, or on prasad, food or offering water.
- Avoid contact with eyes, mouth and skin.
- Test first on a small hidden area of fabric or delicate surfaces.
- Keep away from children and pets.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from sunlight and heat, and close the bottle properly after use.

Pack sizes

- 50 ml: for travel, gifting or small mandirs
- 100 ml: for regular home use, satsang rooms and larger pooja areas

short_description.en: Siddhak dhoop sticks for pooja combo with 4 fragrances, 50 sticks each: Panchgavya, Guggul, Rose and Chandan. Made without charcoal or harsh chemicals, for daily pooja, aarti, havan and meditation.

long_description.en:
Siddhak dhoop sticks for pooja combo brings together four naturally made dhoop sticks, 50 of each: Panchgavya, Guggul, Rose and Chandan (sandalwood). It is made for devotees who want a pure, devotional atmosphere at home for daily pooja, Gita reading, mantra chanting, meditation or yoga.

In Sanatan Dharma, lighting dhoop is a sacred offering: it is the "Dhupa" step of the Shodashopachara (16-step) pooja, and the rising smoke is seen as prayers reaching the divine. Devotees believe pure dhoop cleanses the atmosphere and supports sadhana, bhakti and meditation.

Benefits

- Natural base materials (herbs, woods, resins, plant powders): no charcoal, no harmful chemicals, no synthetic binders
- Softer, more natural, temple-like fragrances, suitable around elders and children and for people sensitive to harsh incense
- A different fragrance for each deity or mood, for example sandalwood for Vishnu / Krishna and guggul for Shiva
- Keeps your daily pooja fresh rather than repetitive
- Many people feel calmer and more focused during prayer and meditation (traditional perspective)

Ideal for

- Morning and evening aarti in the home mandir
- Japa of "Om Namah Shivaya", "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya" or the Gayatri Mantra
- Reading the Gita, Ramayana, Bhagavatam or Upanishads; meditation and pranayama; satsang and kirtan
- Diwali, Dhanteras, Lakshmi Pooja, Navratri, Durga Pooja, Maha Shivratri, Janmashtami, Ram Navami and Ganesh Chaturthi
- Satyanarayan Katha, Griha Pooja, Griha Pravesh, office or shop opening
- Gifting to spiritual family members, newly married couples and friends, at housewarmings and festivals

How to use

- Clean the pooja area and arrange deity photos or murtis, diya, flowers and water.
- Choose a fragrance for the deity, mood or occasion.
- Hold the stick at the bare end and light the coated end with a matchstick or diya.
- Let it burn for a few seconds until the tip glows, then gently blow out the flame.
- Wave the dhoop in a slow circle before the deity, chanting "Om Shanti Shanti Shantihi", "Om Namo Narayanaya" or "Om Gan Ganapataye Namah".
- Place it in a proper stand or fire-safe base where falling ash lands safely, then sit for aarti, japa or meditation.

Safety and storage

- Always place burning dhoop in a stable, non-flammable holder.
- Keep away from curtains, paper, furniture and flammable decor.
- Do not leave dhoop unattended, especially around children or pets.
- Use in a well-ventilated area, particularly in small rooms.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and sunlight, and reseal the pack.

Pack size

- Combo of 4 fragrances × 50 sticks (Panchgavya, Guggul, Rose, Chandan)

long_description.en:
Siddhak kesar dhoop sticks bring the holy fragrance of kesar (saffron) to your daily Vishnu Pooja. They combine pure kesar with a clean, natural base for a soft, soothing aroma that supports focus, devotion and inner calm.

In Sanatan tradition kesar is closely tied to Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi: it is used in Vishnu tilak, offered in prasadam such as kesar kheer, sheera or milk during Vishnu vrats, and its golden colour is linked with abundance, dharma and divine grace. Lighting kesar dhoop before offering flowers, naivedya and deepam completes the dhupa step of the Shodashopachara (16-step) pooja.

Benefits

- Made with pure kesar (saffron) and natural base ingredients for a smooth, clean burn
- Soft, sattvik fragrance, not harsh or heady, for closed home spaces and people sensitive to strong smoke
- Helps create a calm setting for Vishnu Sahasranama, scripture reading or silent meditation
- Welcoming aroma for festivals and guests
- 50 sticks: enough for daily morning and evening pooja plus special occasions

Ideal for

- Daily Vishnu / Lakshmi Narayan pooja and aarti
- Satyanarayan Katha and Vishnu Sahasranama path
- Thursday (Guruvar) pooja for Vishnu and Brihaspati
- Vaikuntha Ekadashi, Dev Uthani Ekadashi, Diwali, Dhanteras, Janmashtami and Ram Navami
- Griha Pravesh and other new beginnings
- Meditation, japa and study of the Gita or Bhagavatam
- Homes, ashrams, small temples, offices and spiritual centres

How to use

- Clean the altar and place the photo or murti of Lord Vishnu / Lakshmi Narayan with flowers, diya, water and prasad.
- Light one end of the dhoop stick with a matchstick or diya flame, let it burn for a few seconds, then gently blow out the flame so it glows.
- Wave the dhoop in a circular motion before the deity (Dhupa Upachara), softly chanting "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya" or "Om Vishnave Namah".
- Place it in a proper stand or on a fire-safe surface, away from flammable materials, and continue with aarti or stotras.

Safety and storage

- Always place a burning dhoop stick in a stable, non-flammable holder on a heat-resistant surface.
- Keep away from children, pets, curtains, paper and other flammable items.
- Use in a well-ventilated area, especially in small rooms.
- Never leave burning dhoop unattended.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight, and keep the pack closed to preserve the fragrance.

Pack size

- 50 sticks

short_description.en: Siddhak organic dhoop masala is a 100 g hand-crafted blend of natural resins, herbs and aromatic woods for pooja, meditation and yoga. Free from charcoal, chemicals and synthetic fragrance; use it in dhoop cups or a dhoop dani.

long_description.en:
Siddhak organic dhoop masala (100 g) is a loose dhoop powder for those who value purity and tradition. Burning natural dhoop is a traditional way to clear heaviness from a room and fill it with a calm, pleasant fragrance, whether at home, in the office, a studio or a spiritual space.

It is made from natural ingredients such as aromatic woods, resins, herbs, flowers and plant powders, with no charcoal, synthetic fillers, artificial fragrance or toxic chemicals. It burns with a softer, more natural aroma, which suits people who find stick incense too harsh.

Benefits

- Traditionally used to dispel negativity and create a light, happy atmosphere
- Supports peace and focus during meditation, mantra chanting, yoga, reading or deep work
- Completes daily aarti, havan or spiritual practice with a natural fragrance
- Chemical-free and gentle on the senses
- Economical: 100 g gives many sessions, and you control how much to use each time (a pinch or a spoonful)
- Effects are based on traditional belief; individual experience may vary

Ideal for

- Daily pooja and aarti, morning and evening
- Meditation and yoga
- Clearing the air after stressful days
- New beginnings: a new home, new job or new project
- Before or after guests and gatherings
- Homes, offices, yoga studios, healing spaces and personal altars

How to use

- With a charcoal tablet: light the tablet in a heat-safe metal or clay burner until it glows, then sprinkle a small pinch of dhoop masala on top. Add more in small amounts as needed.
- On a traditional dhoop burner (dhoop dani): add a thin layer of ash or sand, place a burning ember safely inside, and add a little dhoop masala so it slowly smoulders.
- In an electric dhoop / incense diffuser (if compatible): add a small amount to the tray and switch on as per the device instructions.
- Simple ritual: tidy the room, open a window for a moment, light the dhoop, set an intention ("May this space be filled with peace, love, light and positive energy"), let the fragrance reach every corner and sit quietly for a few moments.

Safety and storage

- Always burn in a heat-resistant holder or burner, in a well-ventilated area.
- Keep away from children, pets, curtains and flammable items, and never leave burning dhoop unattended.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and sunlight, and reseal the pack after each use.

Pack size

- 100 g (organic dhoop powder for dhoop cups / dhoop dani)

- Gomaya (cow dung)
- Gomutra (cow urine)
- Dugdh (milk)
- Dahi (curd)
- Ghee (clarified butter)

Benefits

- 100% cow dung base: pure, dried cow dung (gomaya) as the main base
- Made with the Panchgavya elements and natural herbs, as a symbolic Vedic offering
- Free from charcoal, harsh chemicals and synthetic binders, for a gentler, sattvik smoke
- Warm, earthy, mandir-like fragrance that recalls temples, havans and village poojas
- As per tradition, burning Panchgavya dhoop is said to purify the atmosphere and offering it is considered punya (a matter of faith)
- 50 sticks: enough for daily morning and evening pooja plus festivals

Ideal for

- Daily griha pooja and aarti
- Havan and yajna at home, alongside havan samagri
- Diwali, Navratri, Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi, Shivratri, Ram Navami and Ekadashi
- Satyanarayan Katha, Griha Pravesh, Vastu Pooja and Sankalp poojas
- Meditation, mantra chanting, japa and dhyana
- Gifting for Griha Pravesh, weddings, anniversaries, satsangs and festival visits

How to use

- Clean the altar and arrange your deity idols or photos with diya, flowers, water and prasad.
- Hold one stick at the uncoated end and light the other end with a matchstick or diya.
- Let it burn for a few seconds until the tip glows, then gently blow out the flame.
- Move the dhoop in circles before the deity to complete the dhupa step, chanting "Om Shanti Shanti Shantihi", "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya" or "Om Namah Shivaya" as suits the deity.
- Place it in a dhoop stand on a stable, fire-safe surface and continue your pooja.

Safety and storage

- Always place a burning dhoop stick in a stable, non-flammable holder on a heat-resistant surface.
- Keep away from children, pets, curtains, paper and other flammable items.
- Use in a well-ventilated area, especially in small rooms.
- Never leave burning dhoop unattended.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight, and keep the pack closed to preserve the fragrance.

Pack size

- 50 sticks (Panchgavya / Panchtatva, Siddhak jar)

short_description.en: Siddhak rose dhoop sticks are made from pure cow dung with a soothing rose aroma and no charcoal. For Mata Ji and Ganesh pooja, daily aarti and festivals, in a pack of 50.

long_description.en:
Siddhak rose dhoop sticks blend the sacredness of cow dung (gomaya) with the gentle sweetness of rose. They are made to make Maa Durga, Ambe Maa, Mata Rani and Ganesh pooja feel more complete and devotional.

In Hindu tradition the cow is revered as Gau Mata, and cow dung has been used in havan, yajna and pooja since ancient times. Burning it in a ritual way is traditionally believed to purify the surroundings on a subtle level and invite blessings. Rose (gulab) is offered to Mata Ji as a symbol of love and devotion, and is used in garlands for Ganesh pooja and Ganesh Chaturthi.

Benefits

- Pure cow dung as the main base, with no charcoal added
- Floral, lightly sweet, soothing rose fragrance: not overly strong or artificial
- Feels closer to havan and village-style pooja than a chemical room freshener
- Helps you settle into a devotional mood; pairs well with flowers, kumkum and prasad
- Suits people who prefer sattvik, cow-based products and those sensitive to harsh incense
- 50 sticks: enough for daily aarti plus festivals and vrats

Ideal for

- Navratri, Durga Pooja, Durga Ashtami and Vaishno Devi pooja
- Ambe Maa, Kali Maa and Santoshi Maa pooja; Tuesday and Friday Devi pooja
- Jagran, chowki and bhajan sandhya at home
- Daily Ganesh aarti, Ganesh Chaturthi (sthapana, aarti, visarjan) and Sankashti Chaturthi
- Office, shop and business Ganpati pooja
- Gifting for Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, Diwali, Griha Pravesh, new mandirs, weddings and anniversaries

How to use

- Clean the pooja area and arrange Mata Ji's and Ganesh Ji's idols or photos with diya, water, flowers, kumkum, rice and prasad.
- Hold one stick at the bare end and light the coated tip with a matchstick or diya.
- Let it burn for a few seconds until the tip glows, then gently blow out the flame.
- Wave the dhoop in gentle circles before the deities, chanting "Ya Devi Sarva Bhuteshu..." or "Jai Ambe Gauri" for Mata Ji, and "Om Gan Ganapataye Namah" or "Jai Ganesh Deva" for Ganesh Ji.
- Place it in a dhoop stand on a heat-proof surface and continue with aarti, bhajan or japa.

Safety and storage

- Always place a burning dhoop stick in a stable, non-flammable holder on a heat-resistant surface.
- Keep away from children, pets, curtains, paper and other flammable items.
- Use in a well-ventilated area, especially in small rooms.
- Never leave burning dhoop unattended.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight, and keep the pack closed to preserve the fragrance.

Pack size

short_description.en: Siddhak pure sandalwood dhoop sticks combine a cow dung base with calming chandan (sandalwood) aroma, with no charcoal. For Vishnu Ji Pooja, Lakshmi–Narayan pooja, Satyanarayan Katha and daily aarti, in a pack of 50.

long_description.en:
Siddhak pure sandalwood (chandan) dhoop sticks are made for those who worship Lord Vishnu, Lakshmi–Narayan and his avatars (Ram, Krishna, Narasimha, Vamana). They combine the sacredness of cow dung (gomaya) with the cooling fragrance of sandalwood.

Chandan is one of the most loved offerings to Lord Vishnu: Vishnu murtis and shaligrams are anointed with chandan tilak, and the Vaishnav tilak (urdhva pundra) is traditionally made with sandalwood. Cow dung is used in yajna, havan and agnihotra as a sacred fuel, and burning it in ritual is traditionally believed to purify the surroundings and invite auspiciousness.

Benefits

- Pure cow dung as the primary base, with no charcoal and minimal natural binders
- Soft, mildly sweet, soothing sandalwood fragrance: not sharp, synthetic or overpowering
- Feels more like havan smoke than a perfumed room freshener
- Supports a calm, devotional mood for meditation, mantra chanting and scripture reading
- 50 sticks: enough for daily pooja plus Thursdays, Ekadashi and vrat days

Ideal for

- Daily Vishnu Ji Pooja and Lakshmi–Narayan aarti
- Satyanarayan Katha and Vishnu Sahasranama path
- Ekadashi pooja (including Dev Uthani and Vaikuntha Ekadashi), Janmashtami and Ram Navami
- Thursday (Guruvar) pooja for Vishnu and Brihaspati
- Shravan / Sawan month for combined Vishnu–Shiva worship
- Meditation on "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya" and reading the Gita, Bhagavatam or Vishnu Puran
- Gifting for Griha Pravesh, Vaishnav festivals, Diwali, weddings and anniversaries

How to use

- Clean the altar and place the murti or photo of Lord Vishnu / Lakshmi–Narayan / Krishna / Ram, with diya, water, flowers, tulsi leaves and prasad.
- Hold one stick at the bare end and light the coated end with a match or diya flame.
- Let it burn for a few seconds until a small red ember forms, then gently blow out the flame.
- Wave the dhoop in slow clockwise circles before the deity, chanting "Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya", "Om Vishnave Namah" or a short portion of Vishnu Sahasranama.
- Place it in a dhoop stand on a heat-resistant surface and continue with aarti or bhajans.

Safety and storage

- Always place a burning dhoop stick in a stable, non-flammable holder on a heat-resistant surface.
- Keep away from children, pets, curtains, paper and other flammable items.
- Use in a well-ventilated area, especially in small rooms.
- Never leave burning dhoop unattended.
- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight, and keep the pack closed to preserve the fragrance.

Pack size

- 50 sticks (Sandalwood / Chandan, Siddhak jar)

short_description.en: Siddhak Desi Babool datoon (datun) sticks bring back the age-old Indian way of oral care. Natural Babool (Acacia) twigs that clean teeth and freshen breath without toothpaste or plastic, in a pack of 25.

long_description.en:
Siddhak Desi Babool datoon (datun) sticks are a simple, time-tested way to care for your teeth and gums, just like our elders did. Before plastic toothbrushes and flavoured toothpastes, Indian homes used Babool (Acacia) twigs to keep the mouth clean and fresh.

Babool has traditionally been valued in Ayurveda for oral hygiene. Each stick is 100% natural Babool wood: no foaming agents, no artificial colours, no synthetic flavours.

Benefits

- Natural oral care: the traditional way to gently clean teeth and support gum hygiene
- Chewing the twig releases natural juices that help freshen breath and reduce food deposits
- Eco-friendly and plastic-free: no plastic handle or nylon bristles; completely biodegradable
- Chemical-free routine: no SLS, parabens, artificial sweeteners or synthetic fragrance
- Minimalist: one stick is enough for a full brushing session
- Cost-effective: 25 sticks give many days of use at a low cost per use
- Fits a natural, satvik, Ayurveda-inspired lifestyle

Ideal for

- People who prefer natural and Ayurveda-inspired products
- Anyone cutting down on plastic, and eco-conscious families teaching kids sustainable living
- Yogis, meditators and spiritual seekers
- Bathroom, travel bag, office, farmhouse, village home or ashram
- Religious fasts, rituals and natural-only days

How to use

- Take one stick and gently chew one end until it forms soft, brush-like fibres.
- Clean your teeth in small circular motions and gently massage your gums.
- Spit out any residue and rinse with clean water.
- Cut off the used end and keep the rest for later, or discard the stick after one full use.
- Best used daily in the morning. You can use it alongside your regular brush.
- New to datoon? Start a few times a week to get used to the taste and feel.

Storage

- Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture, and use a fresh stick regularly for hygiene.

Pack size

- 25 sticks (enough for regular use by one person or short-term use by a small family)

short_description.en: Siddhak Multani Mitti is pure, fine-textured Fuller's Earth specially sourced from Bhavnagar, Gujarat. It cleanses pores and absorbs excess oil, for DIY face packs, hair and scalp masks and body ubtan.

long_description.en:
Siddhak Multani Mitti (Fuller's Earth) is specially sourced from Bhavnagar, Gujarat, a region known for fine-textured, mineral-rich clay. It is carefully processed to keep its natural properties and is not blended with low-grade clays.

It is a single ingredient: pure Multani Mitti in natural powder form, free from chemicals, preservatives, colours and added fragrance, and not mixed with talc, chalk or fillers. Its fine texture blends easily with rose water, milk, aloe vera gel or hydrosols, spreads smoothly without feeling gritty and washes off easily.

Benefits for skin

- Deep cleanses pores by drawing out excess oil, sweat and impurities
- Absorbs excess sebum, useful for oily and combination skin
- Gives a fresh, cooling feel on hot, humid days
- Helps reduce the appearance of tan and dullness with regular use
- Supports visibly smoother, clearer-looking skin over time

Benefits for hair and scalp

- Helps remove oil, dirt and product build-up from the scalp
- Leaves hair feeling lighter and cleaner
- Adds a mild natural volume to oily, weighed-down hair
- Mix with curd, aloe vera, amla powder or herbal infusions for a home hair spa
- Benefits are based on traditional use; individual results may vary

How to use

- Classic face pack (normal to oily skin): mix 1–2 teaspoons with enough rose water to make a smooth paste. Apply on a cleansed face and neck, avoiding eyes and lips. Leave for 10–15 minutes until just semi-dry, rinse with lukewarm water and moisturise.
- Glow pack (dull or tanned skin): 1 teaspoon Multani Mitti, 1 teaspoon curd or milk, and an optional pinch of turmeric or sandalwood powder. Leave for 10–15 minutes and rinse. Use 1–2 times a week.
- Dry or sensitive skin pack: 1 teaspoon Multani Mitti with 1–2 teaspoons aloe vera gel and a few drops of honey or facial oil. Do not overuse on very dry skin.
- Hair and scalp mask: 2–3 tablespoons with enough curd, aloe vera juice or herbal tea to make a thick paste. Apply to scalp and hair for 15–20 minutes, then rinse, with a mild shampoo if needed.

Tips

- Always do a patch test before first use.
- Wash off when semi-dry; do not let the mask crack.
- Use 1–3 times a week depending on skin type (less for dry, more for oily), and follow with toner and moisturiser.
- Suitable for women and men of all ages with oily, combination and normal skin. If your skin is very dry or sensitive, use sparingly, mixed with hydrating ingredients.

Storage

- Store in a cool, dry place and keep the pack tightly sealed.
- Use a clean, dry spoon and keep water out of the pack to prevent lumps.

Pack sizes

- 100 g
- 500 g
- 1000 g (1 kg)

short_description.en: Siddhak firewood ash for garden use is 100% natural, chemical-free ash from untreated firewood, rich in potassium, calcium and trace minerals. Mix it into pots, garden beds or compost; available in 500 g and 1 kg packs.

long_description.en:
Siddhak 100% natural firewood ash for garden and farm use is sourced from pure, untreated firewood. Gardeners and farmers use it for its mineral content and its soil pH-balancing and natural pest-repelling properties, whether for vegetables, flowers, indoor plants or fruit trees.

Firewood ash has been used in traditional and modern farming for decades. It contains potassium (K), which supports plant strength, drought tolerance and flowering, along with calcium, magnesium and micronutrients that help maintain soil fertility and strong root development. Our ash is finely powdered so it mixes easily into soil.

Benefits

- 100% natural and chemical-free: from pure firewood with no additives
- Rich in potassium and minerals: supports strong roots, better flowering and healthier growth
- Improves soil structure: aids aeration, reduces acidity and supports microbial activity
- Natural pest repellent: helps keep slugs, ants and harmful insects away
- For all plants: vegetables, fruit trees, flowering plants, indoor pots, terrace gardens and farms
- Eco-friendly and sustainable, finely powdered for easy mixing with soil or compost

How to use

- Pots and indoor plants: mix 1–2 tablespoons into the topsoil once every 2–3 weeks.
- Garden beds: spread a thin layer and mix lightly into the soil before watering.
- Composting: add a small amount to enrich compost with minerals.
- Fruit trees and vegetables: apply around the base to support flowering and yield.
- Avoid excessive use, as too much ash can make soil alkaline.

Pack sizes

- 500 g: for small home gardens, balcony plants and regular care
- 1000 g (1 kg): for large gardens, farms or heavy soil improvement

short_description.en: Siddhak organic manure for plants is a 100% pure, chemical-free, nutrient-rich manure that improves soil health and supports plant growth. Choose 10 kg for home gardens or 50 kg for farms and bulk use.

long_description.en:
Siddhak Pure Organic Manure for plants is a nutrient-rich blend that improves soil fertility and supports healthier, stronger plant growth, for home gardeners and farmers alike.

Unlike chemical fertilisers that give quick results but harm soil over time, organic manure works with nature, improving soil structure, moisture retention and microbial activity. It is slowly decomposed by natural processes to lock in nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium along with essential micronutrients.

Benefits

- 100% organic and chemical-free: safe for all plants, soil types and the environment
- Improves soil structure: better aeration and water-holding capacity
- Boosts microbial activity that supports growth
- Slow, steady nutrient release with no risk of burning plants
- Odour-controlled and professionally cured for indoor and outdoor use
- Helps plants develop stronger roots and greener leaves, for better yield
- An eco-friendly choice for those moving to organic cultivation

Where to use

- Vegetable gardens, kitchen gardens and herbs
- Fruit trees and flowering plants
- Lawns and landscaping
- Potted indoor and outdoor plants
- Organic farming fields and nursery plantations

How to use

- Mix the manure into the topsoil, 1–2 inches deep.
- Use during soil preparation, at planting, or as a regular nutrient booster.
- Apply once every 20–30 days for best results.

Pack sizes

- 10 kg bag: home gardens, terrace gardens, pots, indoor plants, kitchen gardens and small landscaping
- 50 kg bag: farm fields, nurseries, commercial growers, large landscaping and bulk needs
